quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue was $1.25 billion, up 16% sequentially and 28% year over year, with revenue and key profitability metrics at the high end of or above guidance. Reported gross margin was 47.6%, which included about 100 basis points of discrete items mostly from refunds of tariffs and duties. Operating income was approximately $320 million for a 25.6% operating margin, up 480 basis points year over year and well above the guidance midpoint, on operating expenses of $275 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $358 million (28.6% margin), net interest expense $33 million (down from $46 million a year ago), the effective tax rate 19.6%, and net earnings $232 million or $3.30 per diluted share - up 86% year over year per share and above the high end of guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $1.25B (+16% QoQ, +28% YoY); gross margin 47.6%; operating margin 25.6% (+480bps YoY); adjusted EBITDA $358M; EPS $3.30 (+86% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: total revenue of $1.35 billion plus or minus $40 million, split as semiconductor $630 million plus or minus $15 million, Electronics and Packaging $385 million plus or minus $15 million, and Specialty Industrial $335 million plus or minus $10 million. Gross margin is guided to 47% plus or minus 100 basis points, operating expenses $280 million plus or minus $5 million (growing much more slowly than revenue), operating income $355 million for a 26.3% margin, adjusted EBITDA $395 million plus or minus $28 million, and EPS $3.58 plus or minus $0.31. The Q3 tax rate is about 20% with the full year at the lower end of the previously guided 18-20% range, and capex remains 4-5% of revenue for the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $1.35B ±$40M (semi $630M, E&P $385M, specialty industrial $335M); gross margin 47%; EPS $3.58 ±$0.31

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor revenue was $554 million, up 19% sequentially and 28% year over year - a meaningful acceleration from 13% year-over-year growth in Q1 - and the Q3 guide implies year-over-year growth ACCELERATING TO OVER 50%. Within that, CEO John Lee said dep-etch is growing significantly faster than the over-50% average while litho, metrology and inspection have smaller ramp amplitudes; MKS is exposed to 85% of WFE. Full-year semiconductor growth of a little north of 35% was accepted as the right math. Design wins include being the PROCESS TOOL OF RECORD for dissolved gas applications in advanced logic and segment share leadership in RF POWER for high-aspect-ratio dielectric etch. Growth was broad-based across plasma and reactive gases, vacuum, power solutions, optics and photonics, with the last gaining momentum in lithography, metrology and inspection.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor $554M (+19% QoQ, +28% YoY); Q3 implies >50% YoY growth; exposed to 85% of WFE; FY2026 semi growth a little north of 35%

quarterly_data.signal: NAND is turning: MKS saw increased momentum in NAND UPGRADE activity in Q2 and expects it to continue, possibly better. RF power is the LARGEST PART OF THE BILL OF MATERIALS in such an upgrade, which is why MKS benefits disproportionately from upgrades. Announced NAND GREENFIELD fabs are expected to come in towards the END OF 2027 AND BEGINNING OF 2028, which would be even better because MKS would supply the rest of its semiconductor portfolio around a brand-new tool; NAND should become a bigger percentage of semi revenue in 2028. Until then the mix stays largely logic and DRAM driven.
quarterly_data.figure: NAND greenfield fabs expected end-2027 into 2028; NAND to become a bigger share of semi revenue in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics and Packaging revenue was $381 million, up 19% sequentially and 44% year over year, above the high end of the outlook. CHEMISTRY EQUIPMENT DEMAND IS 'EASILY THE STRONGEST IT HAS EVER BEEN,' supported by AI server investments INCLUDING OPTICAL MODULES, and visibility now extends THROUGH 2027 - underwritten by 6-to-9-month equipment lead times that require customer down payments. Chemistry sales rose 21% year over year excluding FX and palladium pass-through. AI-related chemistry has climbed from 5% of total chemistry in 2024 to 10%, then 15% last quarter, and is now put at 15-20%. The chemistry attached per dollar of equipment remains a 20-40% range but should now be modelled at the LOWER end because AI boards require higher-end equipment with higher ASPs. Equipment revenue, historically at most $200 million a year, will be significantly higher this year. Q3 E&P revenue is expected up over 30% year over year, with AI investment partly offset by normal flex seasonality.
quarterly_data.figure: E&P $381M (+19% QoQ, +44% YoY); chemistry +21% YoY ex-FX/palladium; AI chemistry now 15-20% of chemistry (from 5% in 2024); visibility through 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build-out on two fronts. MKS is DOUBLING the capacity of its Guangzhou chemistry equipment factory, which comes ONLINE IN Q3 2027; in the meantime it has turned the Germany factory back on - previously running at a low level, now much busier - and keeps eking out space in the existing Guangzhou plant, so it is 'bursting at the seams' but has been able to take every order. On the semiconductor side the new Malaysia (Penang) supercenter opened in Q2 with first revenue shipments already made; it was not needed for 2026 demand and is ramping for 2027 and beyond, and can be expanded at MKS's option. Management RAISED the WFE level it believes it can support once Penang is filled out to the $200-250 BILLION range, an increase from the $180-200 billion cited last quarter. Start-up costs run through cost of goods at 50-80 basis points of gross margin per quarter for at least the next couple of quarters and are expected to be self-liquidating.
quarterly_data.figure: Guangzhou chemistry equipment capacity doubling, online Q3 2027; supportable WFE raised to $200B-$250B (from $180B-$200B); 50-80bps quarterly gross-margin drag from start-up costs

quarterly_data.signal: Within Electronics and Packaging, FLEX PCB drilling is aimed mostly at smartphones and peripherals - foldables, smartphones, AirPods - and 'not much of it is being used in AI'; it was strong in the first half and is seasonally down in Q3 ahead of the next design cycles. The AI exposure is in RIGID PCB DRILLING, where MKS is seeing increased order activity as the market embraces its differentiated capabilities and cost-of-ownership proposition, driven by two markets: AI and the LOW EARTH ORBIT market. Management also said the mobile demand destruction feared earlier in the year has proved MORE BENIGN than expected. On the chemistry ramp mechanics: it takes 24 to 30 months from equipment going in to volume chemistry, and the majority of today's chemistry growth still comes from PREVIOUSLY INSTALLED capacity, with some customers even turning mothballed tools back on.

Specialty Industrial revenue was $313 million, up 8% sequentially and 14% year over year - the highest level since 2023 - driven by DATACOM (specifically communications testing for AI data centers) and DEFENSE, both expected to stay strong in Q3. Automotive is bouncing along with no degradation or material improvement, and industrial is seeing incremental improvement of a smaller magnitude. Separately, services revenue reached one of the highest levels ever, which management attributes to very high utilisation at semiconductor customers whose fabs have been running hot for a couple of years; management treats this as a new elevated baseline for the foreseeable future.
quarterly_data.figure: Specialty Industrial $313M (+8% QoQ, +14% YoY), highest since 2023

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and capital allocation: MKS closed the quarter with over $1.6 billion of liquidity - $611 million of cash and cash equivalents plus an undrawn $1 billion revolving credit facility - and generated free cash flow of $188 million, about 15% of revenue. Leverage was 3.0x on trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion, DOWN A FULL TURN since Q2 of last year. A $100 million term loan prepayment was made in the week of the call, with additional prepayments being considered for Q3 and Q4; organic growth investment remains the first priority and deleveraging a close second. The quarterly dividend was $0.25 per share, or $17 million, following a 14% increase in Q1. Capex and working capital are both expected to rise through the remainder of the year to support the ramp.
quarterly_data.figure: >$1.6B liquidity; Q2 FCF $188M (~15% of revenue); leverage 3.0x on $1.1B TTM adjusted EBITDA, down a full turn YoY
